questions.question: Which change most strongly raises concern for acute coronary syndrome in a patient with known CCD?
choices: Predictable unchanged exertional symptoms that resolve as usual
New chest pressure at rest or a worsening/prolonged pattern
A stable medication list
A routine exercise question
questions.explanation: New, worsening, prolonged, or rest-related symptoms can represent acute coronary syndrome and require urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Why should an FNP not dismiss chest burning as GERD without further assessment?
choices: Ischemia can be described as burning, pressure, breathlessness, fatigue, or atypical discomfort
GERD never causes burning
Only classic crushing pain is cardiac
Stable vitals rule out every cardiac cause
questions.explanation: Ischemic symptoms are variable; clinical context, change from baseline, associated symptoms, and stability are essential.

questions.question: What is a primary goal of chronic coronary disease care?
choices: Reduce future cardiovascular events while improving symptoms and function
Avoid all physical activity
Use the same medication combination for every patient
Order testing at fixed intervals regardless of symptoms
questions.explanation: CCD care combines risk reduction with symptom relief and quality-of-life improvement.

questions.question: Which component belongs in secondary prevention for CCD?
choices: Lipid, blood-pressure, diabetes, tobacco, activity, and medication-access care
Only annual chest imaging
Ignoring medication cost
Stopping all exercise indefinitely
questions.explanation: Secondary prevention is multifactorial and must include feasible risk-factor and adherence support.

questions.question: What is an appropriate use of cardiac rehabilitation when a patient is eligible?
choices: Support supervised activity, education, and risk-factor modification
Replace all medication review
Delay follow-up after MI
Evaluate acute unstable chest pain at home
questions.explanation: Cardiac rehabilitation can improve recovery, activity, education, and cardiovascular outcomes for eligible patients.

questions.question: Why is medication reconciliation especially important in CCD?
choices: Antiplatelet, anticoagulant, NSAID, supplement, and duplicate-drug exposure can alter ischemic and bleeding risk
It is only necessary after surgery
OTC medications cannot affect care
Every CAD patient uses the same antithrombotic regimen
questions.explanation: The indication and safety of antithrombotic therapy are individualized, and OTC or duplicate agents can cause harm.

questions.question: Which issue requires special safety counseling with nitroglycerin?
choices: Potential interaction with phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors
Need for routine antibiotic prophylaxis
Use as a substitute for emergency evaluation in all chest pain
It eliminates the need to assess blood pressure
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin has important interaction and hypotension safety considerations; patients need individualized instructions.

questions.question: When is routine periodic ischemic or anatomic testing generally not the main strategy?
choices: A stable patient without clinical or functional change
New progressive angina
New acute dyspnea with concerning findings
A changed symptom pattern
questions.explanation: In stable CCD without a change in status, routine repeat testing is not a replacement for appropriate longitudinal assessment.

questions.question: When is expedited cardiology referral reasonable in CCD?
choices: New/progressive angina, uncertain diagnosis, uncontrolled symptoms, or new heart-failure/arrhythmia findings
A fully stable baseline visit with no questions
Only after a patient declines all therapy
Never after prior PCI
questions.explanation: Changing symptoms, uncertainty, uncontrolled disease, and complex comorbidity can warrant timely cardiology involvement.

questions.question: What is the FNP-level CCD principle?
choices: Treat a historical stent as the entire diagnosis
Integrate symptom trajectory, acute safety, prevention, medication access, and follow-up
Assume symptom absence means risk is gone
Use a test result without considering function
questions.explanation: High-quality CCD care protects against acute ischemia while addressing long-term risk and practical barriers.
